issues.description: Method name inconsistency: The problem statement (UML and text) requires a public method named checkOrderReady() in class SealSaloon. The solution implementation provides a method named processOrders() that contains the order-serving logic but does not provide a public checkOrderReady() method. This naming mismatch (checkOrderReady() vs processOrders()) can confuse students and cause test harnesses or instructions that expect checkOrderReady() to fail or be unclear about which method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent with the problem statement: either rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (keeping its signature and behavior), or add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders(). Update any references in tests, the problem description, and examples so all artifacts call the same method name.

issues.description: The exercise asks for a method that processes and serves queued orders. In the problem statement and UML this method is named checkOrderReady(). In the solution implementation (SealSaloon.java) the same behavior is implemented in a method named processOrders(). This identifier mismatch (checkOrderReady() vs processOrders()) maps the same concept to different names and can confuse students: they may implement or look for checkOrderReady() as specified in the task and UML but find processOrders() in the provided solution, making it harder to compare implementations or understand the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifiers so the conceptual method name is consistent. Either: (A) Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() and update internal calls accordingly; or (B) add a public checkOrderReady() method in SealSaloon that delegates to the existing processOrders() method (checkOrderReady() { processOrders(); }). This preserves the API named in the problem/UML while keeping the solution logic intact.
